la:noun:mysterium.html:
mystērĭum, ii, n., = μυστήριον,
a secret service, secret rites, secret worship of a deity, divine mystery (class.; cf. arcanum).
Lit., of the mysteries of Ceres, otherwise called sacra Eleusinia, ; : mysteria Attica,: mysteria Cereris initiorum enuntiare,: mysteria facere,to celebrate the sacred mysteries,.—Also, the festival on which these mysteries were celebrated: in quem diem Romana incidant mysteria, the festival of the goddess Bona Dea, ; sq.—
Transf., in gen., a secret thing, secret, mystery: rhetorum mysteria,; : epistolae nostrae tantum habent mysteriorum,: accipe congestas, mysteria frivolas nugas,.—
(Eccl. Lat.)
Something transcending mere human intelligence: mysterium evangelii,: mysterium sicut evangelizaverat per prophetas,: mysteria regni caelorum,.—
Of Antichrist, : mysterium iniquitatis,. —
The Lord's supper: mysterium celebrat, Cor. 11, 27.

la:noun:myrtus.html:
myrtus (murtus), i and ūs, f., = μύρτος,
a myrtle, myrtle-tree, : viridi caput impedire myrto,.—Poet., for a spear of myrtle-wood: et pastoralem praefixā cuspide myrtum,.—Nom. plur. myrtūs, .—As masc., .—Anteclass. also, myrta or murta, ae, f.: murta nigra,.—Murtus for myrtus: murti nigrae baccae,.

la:other:Mycenae.html:
Mўcēnae, ārum, or Mўcēna, ae, and Mўcēne, ēs, f., = Μυκηναι, Μυκήνη,
a celebrated city in Argolis, of which Agamemnon was king: Agamemnoniaeque Mycenae,; ; : deprensus urbe Mycenae,: Diti sacrata,: ante Agamemnoniam ... Mycenen,.—
Derivv.
Mўcēnaeus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Mycenæ, Mycenæan: ductor,i. e. Agamemnon,: teque, Mycenaeo, Phoebas, amata duci,i. e. Cassandra, beloved by Agamemnon, king of Mycenæ,: manus, i. e. Agamemnonis,: rates,the Grecian fleet, under the command of Agamemnon,.—
Mўcēnensis, e, adj., of or belonging to Mycenæ, Mycenæan.—In plur.: Mўcēnenses, ĭum, m., the inhabitants of Mycenæ, the Mycenæans, Cic. poët. Fin. 2, 6, 18.—
Mўcēnis, ĭdis, f., the Mycenæan, i. e. Iphigenia, daughter of Agamemnon: suppositā fertur mutāsse Mycenida cervā,.

id.
,

Lit.: myrtea silva,: corona,; cf.: myrtea corona (Papirius) usus est, quod Sardos in campis Myrteis superāsset, Paul. ex Müll.: oleum,.—Also, absol.: myr-tĕum, i, n., myrtle-oil, : vinum,.—

Myrtle-colored, chestnutbrown: gausapila,.—
Olea murtea, a kind of olive-tree, .—
Subst.: Myrtĕa, ae, f., the goddess to whom the myrtle is sacred, i. e. Venus, .

mystĭcus, a, um, adj., = μυστικός,
of or belonging to secret rites or mysteries, mystic, mystical (poet.): mystica sacra Dindymenes,: vannus Iacchi,: vitis,: lampas,.—In plur. subst.: mystĭ-ca, ōrum, n., things pertaining to secret rites, ; .—Hence, adv.: mystĭcē, mystically (post-class.), ; .

la:noun:mystagogus.html:
mўstăgōgus, i, m., = μυσταγωγός,
one who conducts a person through secret and sacred places as a guide, an initiator, a mystagogue, .— Trop.: amicitiae meae, te mystagogo usus, accessit,the founder,.

la:other:Mysia.html:
Mȳsĭa, ae, f., = Μυσία,
a country of Asia Minor, divided into Lesser Mysia, on the Hellespont, and Greater Mysia, on the Ægean Sea, ; ; ; ; ; .—
Derivv.
Mȳ-sĭcus, a, um, adj., for Mysius, Mysian (post-Aug.): scammonium,.—
Mȳsĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Mysia, Mysian (class.): homo,.—
Mȳsus, a, um, adj., = Μυσός, of or belonging to Mysia, Mysian: Mysus juvenis,i. e. Telephus, king of Mysia,: dux, the same,: Căīcus,.—Subst.: Mysus aut Phryx,; .—In plur.: Mȳsi, ōrum, m., the inhabitants of Mysia, the Mysians: si quis despicatui ducitur, ut Mysorum ultimus esse dicatur,; ; .
